topic: Social paediatrics: Recognising child abuse and neglect

slides.title: Child Abuse & Neglect: Spot It, Don't Miss It
slides.subtitle: History red flags, TEN-4-FACESp, fractures, head trauma, workup & POCSO duties

slides.title: 4 Types to Know
slides.subtitle: Often more than one in the same child
points: **Neglect**: failure to meet basic needs; the **commonest** form
**Physical abuse**: bruises, burns, fractures, abusive head trauma
**Emotional abuse**: rejection, terrorising, exposure to violence
Also: **fabricated or induced illness** (Munchausen by proxy)
slides.highlight: Neglect is the most common form, and the easiest to overlook.

slides.title: History Red Flags
slides.subtitle: When the story doesn't fit the injury
points: Mechanism **doesn't match** the injury or the child's development
Injury blamed on a **sibling** or the child themselves
slides.highlight: Those who don't cruise rarely bruise: any bruise in a non-mobile infant is a red flag.

slides.title: Bruises: TEN-4-FACESp
slides.subtitle: Bruising rule for children under 4 years
points: **4**: in a child **< 4 years**, or **any bruise** at **< 4 months**
Rule out: Mongolian spots, bleeding disorders, cupping/coining
slides.highlight: Accidental bruises sit over bony prominences: shins, knees, forehead.

slides.title: Fractures & Burns
slides.subtitle: High specificity for abuse
slides.highlight: Rule out osteogenesis imperfecta: blue sclerae, wormian bones, family history.

slides.title: Abusive Head Trauma
slides.subtitle: Commonest cause of abuse deaths in infants
points: Presents as vomiting, irritability, poor feeding, **seizures**, apnoea
Retinal bleeds: **multilayered**, extending to the periphery
Easily misdiagnosed as gastroenteritis or sepsis
slides.highlight: Unexplained encephalopathy in an infant: think AHT, get neuroimaging and fundoscopy.

slides.title: Workup
slides.subtitle: Look for hidden injuries, rule out mimics
points: **Skeletal survey** in all **< 2 years**; repeat in ~2 weeks
slides.highlight: Document exactly: body map, measurements, photos, the carer's own words.

slides.title: Your Duty in India
slides.subtitle: Protect first, then report
points: **POCSO**: reporting suspected sexual abuse is **mandatory** (Sec 19); failure is punishable (Sec 21)
Inform police / SJPU and the **Child Welfare Committee**
**Admit** if the child is unsafe at home
slides.highlight: You don't need proof to report. Reasonable suspicion is enough.

slides.title: Save this. It might save a child 🔖
slides.subtitle: Follow @paediatrick_or_treats for PG notes
points: Share with your casualty & ward team
Comment the red flag you have seen most often

caption:
Child abuse and neglect: the red flags every paediatric resident must spot 🛡️

📋 Types: neglect (commonest) · physical · sexual · emotional · fabricated/induced illness
🚩 History: delay in care · changing story · mechanism doesn't fit development · blamed on sibling · repeated visits
🔍 TEN-4-FACESp: bruising of torso, ears, neck in < 4 yr, any bruise < 4 months, frenulum, angle of jaw, cheeks, eyelids, subconjunctiva, patterned
🦴 High-specificity fractures: metaphyseal corner, posterior rib, scapula, sternum, spinous process, multiple of different ages
🧠 Abusive head trauma: < 1 yr, SDH + multilayered retinal haemorrhages + encephalopathy, often no external injury
🧪 Workup: skeletal survey < 2 yr (repeat ~2 wk), neuroimaging, fundoscopy, coagulation, screen siblings
⚖️ India: POCSO mandatory reporting (Sec 19), CWC, Childline 1098. Reasonable suspicion is enough.

Save 🔖 & share with your team.

For medical education. Verify with current guidelines and your unit protocol.
references: AAP Clinical report: evaluation of suspected child physical abuse
Pierce et al., TEN-4-FACESp (JAMA Netw Open 2021)
